question.text: Which keyword is used to create a class in Java?
question.explanation: The 'class' keyword defines a new class in Java.

question.text: What does OOP stand for?
question.explanation: OOP stands for Object Oriented Programming.

question.text: In Java, a class can extend more than one class at the same time.
question.explanation: Java does not support multiple inheritance. A class can only extend one parent class.

question.text: Which collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
question.explanation: HashSet implements the Set interface which does not allow duplicates.

question.text: The 'static' keyword means the method belongs to the class, not an instance.
question.explanation: Static methods belong to the class itself and can be called without creating an object.

question.text: What is the correct way to declare an ArrayList in Java?
question.explanation: The correct modern way is ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>() using generics.

question.text: ArrayList is faster than LinkedList for random access by index.
question.explanation: ArrayList uses an array internally so index access is O(1). LinkedList must traverse nodes making it O(n).

question.text: Which interface must a class implement to be used in a for-each loop?
question.explanation: The Iterable interface requires implementing iterator() which enables the for-each loop.

question.text: What is the output of: System.out.println(10 + 20 + "Java")?
question.explanation: 10+20 evaluates to 30 first (both ints), then 30+"Java" concatenates to "30Java".

question.text: In Java, the main method must always be declared as public static void.
question.explanation: The JVM calls main() from outside the class (public), without creating an object (static), and expects no return value (void).

question.text: Which OOP principle hides internal implementation details?
question.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods and restricts direct access to internal state using private fields.

question.text: What does the 'abstract' keyword on a method mean?

options.option: The method runs automatically at startup
The method has no body and must be overridden by subclasses
The method cannot be called from outside

question.explanation: An abstract method has no implementation body. Any non-abstract subclass must provide the implementation.

question.text: Polymorphism allows one method name to behave differently based on the object calling it.
question.explanation: Polymorphism means many forms. The same method name can produce different results depending on the actual object type at runtime.

question.text: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
question.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used to create a subclass that inherits from a parent class.

question.text: An abstract class can have both abstract and non-abstract methods.
question.explanation: Abstract classes can have a mix of abstract methods (no body) and concrete methods (with body). Only interfaces require all methods to be abstract (before Java 8).

question.text: What is method overriding in Java?

options.option: Defining two methods with the same name in the same class
A subclass providing its own implementation of a parent class method
Calling a method from a parent class using super
Making a method private so it cannot be accessed

question.explanation: Overriding is when a subclass redefines a method from the parent class with the same signature but different behavior.

question.text: Which of these best describes Abstraction?

options.option: Copying properties from parent to child class
Hiding unnecessary details and showing only essential features
Having multiple methods with the same name
Wrapping data and methods together in a class

question.explanation: Abstraction means hiding complex implementation details and exposing only what is necessary to the outside world.

question.text: In Java, a child class automatically gets all public and protected methods of its parent class.
question.explanation: Inheritance means the child class gets all public and protected members of the parent class without rewriting them.

question.text: What is the purpose of the 'super' keyword in Java?

options.option: To create a new object of the parent class
To call a method or constructor from the parent class
To prevent a class from being inherited

question.explanation: super() calls the parent constructor, and super.methodName() calls a parent method from inside a subclass.

question.text: An interface in Java can contain instance variables with values.
question.explanation: Interfaces can only have public static final constants, not regular instance variables. All fields in an interface are implicitly public static final.
